name: cstar-ocean
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.15.1"
  python_min: "3.12"

recipe:
  name: cstar-ocean-suite
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/c/cstar-ocean/cstar_ocean-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: a39f42caca94175037c9ca4a014ed7b5ac9e39a64a1f6e5de522212ab1015163

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - package:
      name: cstar-ocean
      version: ${{ version }}

    build:
      # noarch; not solvable on Windows today (roms-tools -> xesmf/esmf has no
      # win-64 build) but will work there as soon as the deps become available
      noarch: python
      script:
        - python -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
        # activate.d/deactivate.d hooks (recipe/activate.sh has the rationale):
        # PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 on activation keeps the env off Python's user-site
        # (~/.local), which otherwise precedes site-packages on sys.path and
        # silently shadows it -- a chronic breakage on HPC systems where a module
        # Python shares ~/.local. Carried over from the cstar-forge recipe, whose
        # users (the wizard/Jupyter path in particular) hit this; now everyone does.
        - mkdir -p "$PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/deactivate.d"
        - cp "$RECIPE_DIR/activate.sh" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d/cstar-ocean_pythonnousersite.sh"
        - cp "$RECIPE_DIR/deactivate.sh" "$PREFIX/etc/conda/deactivate.d/cstar-ocean_pythonnousersite.sh"
      python:
        entry_points:
          - cstar = cstar.cli.cli:main

    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=61.0.0
        - wheel
        - setuptools-scm >=7.0
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - fakeredis <2.35
        - networkx >=3.6.1
        - psutil >=7.2.2
        - pydantic >=2.13
        - pydantic-settings >=2.13
        - python-dateutil >=2.8.2
        - pytimeparse >=1.1.8
        - python-dotenv
        - pyyaml >=6.0,<7
        - f90nml >=1.4
        - numpy >2.0,<2.4
        - roms-tools >=5.1,<6
        - typer <=0.25
        # -- the forge domain-generation application (cstar.applications.forge),
        #    merged from cstar-forge; mirrors [project.dependencies] --
        - jinja2
        - pandas
        - copernicusmarine
        - gdown
        - dask
        - distributed
        - threadpoolctl
        - numba
        - fsspec
        - kerchunk
        - nest-asyncio
        - ujson
        - fastparquet
        - xarray
        # -- the blueprint wizard (cstar.wizard; `cstar forge wizard` runs it
        #    under voila, `cstar forge copy-notebook` under jupyterlab) --
        - ipywidgets
        - voila
        - jupyterlab
        # matplotlib-base (not the `matplotlib` GUI metapackage): notebooks
        # render via the inline/Agg backends; keeps pyqt out of the default install.
        - matplotlib-base
        - ipython
      run_constraints:
        # copernicusmarine 2.4.x's conda-forge package under-pins click
        # (>=8.0.4,<8.3) relative to its own wheel metadata (>8.2.0,!=8.3.0,
        # !=8.3.1), so an unconstrained solve can pick click 8.1.x and fail
        # `pip check`. Constrain to the intersection; drop once the
        # copernicusmarine feedstock aligns its pin.
        - click >8.2.0,<8.3.0

    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - cstar
            # forge application (pulls roms-tools/dask/kerchunk: a real dependency
            # smoke test), catalog, wizard (import-light) and the CLI group
            - cstar.applications.forge
            - cstar.catalog
            - cstar.wizard
            - cstar.cli.forge
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - script:
          - cstar --version
          - cstar forge --help
          - cstar env register-kernel --help

    about:
      homepage: https://www.cworthy.org
      repository: https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/C-Star
      documentation: https://c-star.readthedocs.io
      summary: Computational systems for tracking ocean carbon
      description: |
        C-Star automates the setup and execution of reproducible ocean-carbon
        modeling workflows (ROMS-MARBL and related regional ocean/biogeochemistry
        simulations) via a blueprint-driven, orchestration-aware Python API and
        command-line tool.
      license: Apache-2.0
      license_file: LICENSE

  - package:
      name: cstar-ocean-standalone
      version: ${{ version }}

    build:
      # metapackage (no code): the toolchain deps below resolve to their
      # platform-specific variants at install time
      noarch: generic

    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("cstar-ocean", exact=True) }}
        - c-compiler
        - cxx-compiler
        - fortran-compiler
        - make
        - cmake
        # mpich-mpicc/mpich-mpifort pin the exact mpich build plus the
        # activation package providing the compiler its wrappers hardcode;
        # bare mpich + raw compilers 2.0 can otherwise solve to a broken
        # mpicc on osx-arm64 (conda-forge/mpich-feedstock#142)
        - mpich
        - mpich-mpicc
        - mpich-mpifort
        - netcdf-fortran
        - libpnetcdf
        # ucla-roms Makefiles require GNU-flavored rsync; macOS system rsync lacks the needed flags
        - rsync

    tests:
      - script:
          # the point of this metapackage is a working toolchain next to cstar
          - cstar --version
          - gfortran --version
          - mpirun --version
          # these exec the wrappers' underlying compilers, catching a broken
          # mpicc/mpif90 (conda-forge/mpich-feedstock#142)
          - mpicc --version
          - mpif90 --version
          - cmake --version
          - make --version
          - rsync --version
          - nf-config --version

    about:
      homepage: https://www.cworthy.org
      repository: https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/C-Star
      documentation: https://c-star.readthedocs.io
      summary: >-
        C-Star with a full conda-provided build toolchain for laptops/workstations
        (HPC users should use system modules instead)
      license: Apache-2.0
      license_file: LICENSE

about:
  homepage: https://www.cworthy.org
  repository: https://github.com/CWorthy-ocean/C-Star
  documentation: https://c-star.readthedocs.io
  summary: Computational systems for tracking ocean carbon
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: LICENSE

extra:
  # multi-output recipe: infrastructure needs the feedstock name to be explicit
  feedstock-name: cstar-ocean
  recipe-maintainers:
    - ScottEilerman
